body.p: , after , , , , , . src/xslt_lower_template.c, src/evaluator_template.c, tests/evaluator_template_test.c; APPLY_TEMPLATES, the one reserved IR extension point of XSLT, is accepted by the verifier. No other IR kind, no public header.

item.p: IR (src/ir_internal.h, the reserved part, completed): sxml_ir_apply_templates = select (NONE: the function's focus, for next-match and apply-imports), mode (0: the current mode), rule search (FROM_START, AFTER_CURRENT_RULE, IMPORTED_ONLY), and three atoms: parameters and tunnel_parameters, two maps from xs:QName to values, and separator (6.7). The by-name parameter binding list is gone (maps replace it). A template rule gains lowest_imported_precedence (the import subtree of its stylesheet level, for apply-imports, 6.11); a mode gains and fails_on_multiple_match. Adders sxml_ir_unit_add_template_rules, _add_modes; accessors _get_mode, _get_template_rules; the text form prints search and maps. Verifier: modes in range, match functions of arity 1, template functions of arity 5.

Template function: one IR function per xsl:template with five parameters: item()?, position, size (its focus slots) and the two parameter maps. Its body binds each xsl:param from map:contains/map:get (coerced, XTTE0590) or its default (select, content as a temporary tree without as, "" or () implicitly, XTDE0700 when mandatory), checks xsl:context-item (XTTE3090, XTTE0590), and coerces the result to as (TRY_CATCH mapping XPTY0004 to XTTE0505). A named template has a second function lowered with an absent focus, called where the caller's focus is absent (xsl:function, the initial template without a global context item: the main function tests the focus with a TRY_CATCH of XPDY0002), so reading . there raises XPDY0002 (10.1.2).

Instructions: xsl:call-template is a STATIC_CALL (XTSE0650, XTSE0680 unless version < 2.0, XTSE0690); xsl:apply-templates, next-match, apply-imports are APPLY_TEMPLATES. Tunnel parameters (10.1.6): inside a template's function its received tunnel map (slot 5) with the tunnel xsl:with-param values put in (map:put), else the empty map. next-match and apply-imports pass the received non-tunnel map too when their effective version is 4.0 or more (6.11). Lexically outside a template body (another focus or function): XTDE0560 when evaluated. apply-templates without select: XNode child::node(), JNode child::, map/array jtree(.)/child::, else XTTE0510.

Modes (6.9): the unnamed mode is mode 1; then every mode xsl:mode declares (XTSE0545 over all its attributes, XTSE0020 for a non-private unnamed mode, XTSE4005, XTSE4010 for enclosing modes) and every mode a template, apply-templates or default-mode names (XTSE3085 under declared-modes). Rules per mode (#all: every mode but enclosing ones) sorted by precedence, priority (explicit or 's default) and declaration order (6.8), heapsort. XTSE0660, XTSE0080.

Built-in templates (6.10) are template functions lowered from short XPath snippets and the existing kinds (APPLY_TEMPLATES in the current mode with the received maps, TEXT_CONSTRUCTOR, SHALLOW_COPY with copy-namespaces, RAISE XTDE0555), one per on-no-match used; shallow-copy-all reads as shallow-copy.

Evaluator (src/evaluator_template.c): a part task per APPLY_TEMPLATES; each match function and template function is a CALL on the machine (no C recursion, : 100,000 levels tested); the task catches errors while a match function runs (6.5: no match); the dynamic context's current_mode and current_template_rule_index are set around each template call and restored on return and on unwinding; on-multiple-match="fail" checks the tied rules (XTDE0540).

Entry: sxml_xslt_lower_initial_template lowers templates and modes, then the invocation (sxml_xslt_invocation): a call of the initial template (xsl:initial-template or a named one) with the global context item, or apply-templates to it in the initial mode (default mode of the principal module; XTDE0045 for an unknown one; XTDE0040 for an unknown initial template). A simplified module is applied in the unnamed mode.
Left out: xsl:sort in apply-templates (4.9), current() and fn:apply-templates (4.10), mode as/typed, warnings, packages (xsl:override, visibility beyond XTSE0020), the 4.0 JNode shallow copy.

Measured with a scratch harness (lower, evaluate, serialize; assertions through the XPath API) over the applicable in-scope cases of the sets of the packet: 316 of 615 pass (match 93/193, mode 70/162, tunnel 53/58, declared-modes 14/14, apply-templates 27/39, next-match 28/51, call-template 21/42, built-in-templates 4/5, template 5/6, apply-imports 1/5, priority 0/40). Of the rest, 99 need global variables (4.7), 73 other instructions, 59 stylesheet parameters (4.7, 4.15), 21 packages, 18 XSLT functions (current, document, xsl:function: 4.10, 4.12), 11 ~T patterns (). Patterns with predicates select the step again from its parent (), so many sibling rules cost quadratic time (match-242: 60 s in a debug build).
